cameraView: ground-level rock drift toward distant mesas

featureReviews.notes: Broad overlapping erosion remnants now have broken rims, caprock ledges, recessed cliff bands, talus shoulders, varied profiles, and distance fade. No mass reads as a primitive cylinder or clean trapezoid.
Three batched continuous-sculpt shapes provide distinct slab, wedge, and high-crown silhouettes with per-instance scale, tilt, and rust/tan/gray tint.
Transforms follow the analytic terrain normal and bury the darker base ring; no point-balanced or floating rocks are visible in the review view.
Wave-interference masks create drifts and open sand. The result is intentionally less uniformly dense than the reference screenshot.
Horizon remains one merged draw; rubble and gravel remain one draw each despite multiple stored geometries. Opaque sorting is disabled and per-object frustum culling is enabled.

knownLimitations: Distant geology is a regionally grounded procedural approximation, not a survey reconstruction of the private site.
The supplied screenshot and final review use similar but not identical free-camera positions.
Headless browser FPS is not treated as representative hardware performance; draw calls, visible triangles, batch structure, and build output are the reliable checks.
summary: The refinement clears the 0.7 acceptance threshold on every critical feature. The remaining camera and density differences do not undermine the requested quality/performance goal.
